name: Anti-establishment
summary: Anti-establishment names opposition to the conventional social, political and economic order and to the elites who run it. Scholarship treats it as an orientation or political style, a divide between 'the people' and the establishment, that cuts across left and right and carries no fixed policy programme.
scope: The orientation as political science defines it (Abedi 2002, Uscinski et al.): hostility to the political establishment, independent of left-right content. It excludes the populist, agrarian-populist, left-wing or right-wing movements that use the label (Omaha Platform, populism), whose texts are other subjects'.
